plain_summary: Review selected oral sedative and systemic CYP3A inhibitor pairs at age 65 or older.

medicine_groups.name: Oral sedatives
medicine_groups.note: Require an oral route. For midazolam, check the ingredient and an explicitly oral sedative formulation. No swallowed midazolam brand was verified for this group. Exclude injection ampoules. Pair oral zolpidem only with systemic clarithromycin.

medicine_groups.name: Systemic strong CYP3A inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Use systemic forms only. Itraconazole counts only with oral alprazolam, midazolam or zopiclone.

rule_for_models: At age ≥65 review oral alprazolam, midazolam or zopiclone with systemic clarithromycin or itraconazole. Add zolpidem with clarithromycin only. When a qualifying pair could overlap and age at supply is unknown, report only a possible finding and ask whether the patient was 65 or older at that supply. Give no finding below age 65. Exclude zolpidem with itraconazole and exclude triazolam. Check the inhibitor course from its start date, quantity and directions. Use an explicit course length when given. If when-needed or as-directed use leaves it possible that the sedative was taken during that course, report only a possible finding. Ask on which nights the patient took the sedative during the course, how much they took and whether it caused unusual drowsiness. Cite both supplies when a qualifying pair overlaps, whatever the indication. Give no finding for a completed switch without overlap.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish actual use, indication or a prescriber’s intent. Treatment and assessments elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm the patient was 65 or older at supply if their age is unclear? If so, could you review the risk of excess sedation during the overlapping courses? For zolpidem, this check applies only to clarithromycin.
